title: Tabulated source index
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes, let $n,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $z$ be a finite bit string, and let $\rho$ assign a natural number to each of eleven registers. Suppose $\rho(r_{\mathrm{NC}})=n$ and $\rho(r_{\mathrm{Z}})=|z|$. Let $s$ be a source descriptor, and write $b_s$ for the bit source obtained from $s$ and $\rho$, and $e_s$ for the linear register expression associated with $s$ and $M$. Assume that $s$ is available: if it is an input-head source, then $\rho(r_{\mathrm{PA}})<\rho(r_{\mathrm{Z}})$; if it is a previous-block source with direction $d\in\{0,1,2\}$, then $1\leq\rho(r_{\mathrm{Q}})+d$; if it is a current-block source, then $1\leq\rho(r_{\mathrm{I}})$; and if it is a previous-snapshot source, then $1\leq\rho(r_{\mathrm{LB}})$. Constant, unary-input, and cell-end sources are always available. If $b_s$ is valid for input length $|z|+n$, output width $\operatorname{cfgWidth}(M)$, and instruction index $i$, then the tabulated index of $b_s$ equals the value of $e_s$ under $\rho$.
